paragraphs: Here's the big idea, baker: God's promise is as certain as God Himself. He had no one greater to swear by, so He swore by Himself (Hebrews 6:13). He did it so we would know the "unchanging nature of His purpose" (Hebrews 6:17). When the One who made everything puts His own name behind a promise, the argument is over.

So what do you do with that when life gets long and the waiting gets loud? You hold on. The writer says there are two unchangeable things in which it is "impossible for God to lie," so we who have fled to take hold of the hope may be "strongly encouraged" (Hebrews 6:18). Your hope doesn't rest on how strong your grip feels today. It rests on a God who cannot lie, and I'm telling you, that is a LOT better than resting on my promise of ten minutes.

And that hope has an anchor, friend. It is "firm and secure," and it reaches the inner sanctuary behind the curtain, where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf (Hebrews 6:19-20). He didn't just go in first. He became a high priest forever (Hebrews 6:20). So when your soul starts drifting, look to where Jesus already is, because He is not going anywhere.
